en.title: The Witcher 3 Remastered has been announced
en.description: A remaster of The Witcher 3 has been announced. The free upgrade will be available next month.
en.fullContent:
A remaster of The Witcher 3 has been announced. The free upgrade will be available next month.

The Witcher 3 Remastered will be released on September 29. The game will be released on all platforms, and for the first time on BattleNet.

Announced during Opening Night Live at Gamescom, the project makes sweeping upgrades to the 2015 RPG.  The remaster will include visual upgrades, both previous expansions, and more quality-of-life fixes.

You can watch the first trailer for The Witcher 3 Remastered below.

The Witcher 3 Remastered will also feature enhanced combat, enhanced traversal, and new SFX for certain powers. The in-game skill tree has also received a revamp, and transmogrification is also being added as part of the update. New combat finishers added.

Players who bought the base version of the game will also get the free upgrade, and they will also receive both previous expansions for free.

en.title: 'GTA VI' Cyberleek update: Everything leaked Tuesday, this week
en.description: Alleged clips of Grand Theft Auto VI simply cannot stop leaking onto the internet.
en.fullContent:
Alleged clips of Grand Theft Auto VI simply cannot stop leaking onto the internet.

After a few clips came out over the weekend and into Monday, there are now a few more, courtesy of the now-notorious leaker known as Cyberleek. As Rockstar and Take-Two step up their efforts to find and stop Cyberleek, clips keep coming out at an even more rapid pace.

We're not going to embed or link directly to any of these clips, but they are easy to find on social media. As of Tuesday morning, three new clips have surfaced:

A clip of protagonist Jason riding a bicycle on a beach packed with civilian NPCs

A clip of Jason looking around a fictional video game retailer, complete with a bunch of fake video game boxes

That brings the total number of leaked clips to 13, at the time of publication. To be clear, their authenticity has not been totally verified, but Rockstar and parent company Take-Two's legal efforts to stop them from coming out is certainly telling in that regard. In subpoenas, Take-Two has referred to the Cyberleek videos as "stolen content" and "leaked gameplay videos," suggesting they could be authentic.

en.title: What to know about the big ‘Grand Theft Auto’ leaks
en.description: This is read by an automated voice. Please report any issues or inconsistencies here.
en.fullContent:
This is read by an automated voice. Please report any issues or inconsistencies here.

See more from the L.A. Times in Google Search.   Set us as preferred

In the video game world, it’s one of the biggest releases of 2026.

For years, fans have been eagerly awaiting the sixth installment to the “Grand Theft Auto” franchise.

But the much-anticipated release of the game has been disrupted by a flurry of leaked scenes — such as a plane flying over a metropolis and the interior of a strip club — that has flooded the internet in the last week without the consent of its publisher, Rockstar Games.

Rockstar has not confirmed the videos’ authenticity, but its parent company, Take-Two Interactive, is taking action. The New York-based company late last week issued subpoenas to Microsoft, Discord, X and Google to track down the alleged hackers.

en.title: Highly anticipated ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ leaked by hacker days ahead of big Netflix preview, games confab in Germany
en.description: The leak of “Grand Theft Auto VI” before the video game’s release later this year — and a planned exclusive preview on Netflix this Thursday — migh...
en.fullContent:
The leak of “Grand Theft Auto VI” before the video game’s release later this year — and a planned exclusive preview on Netflix this Thursday — might seem like a nightmare scenario for the highly secretive developer Rockstar Games.

But it’s more of a bummer for the hush-hush game’s creators than a hit to Rockstar’s bottom line, gamers say — even as Rockstar parent Take-Two’s stock slid as a result of the leaks.

While the latest “Spider-Man” movie is being vaunted as the hit of the summer with over $2.2 billion at the global box office to date, “GTA VI” is expected to bring in “$3.25 billion and $5.2 billion in week-one launch revenue” when it’s released in November, a tracking expert told Forbes last month.

But since then, a hacker — or group — calling themselves Cyberleek, has been releasing peeks of the game since Wednesday. Rockstar, which has not released a new game since 2018, reportedly took legal action in federal court on Friday to get the clips taken down and try to unmask the leaker, reports said.

The way the leaks have been presented indicates the hackers have a complete build of the game — as they were even spelling the group’s name in bullet holes on a wall, meaning they have a playable model, not just a video leak. (FWIW, the hackers have said they’re protesting the fact that Rockstar is not putting out a physical disc for the upcoming game and going digital only, among other gripes.)

Weeks before the leaks, Rockstar announced it was taking the unusual step of showing a special “extended look” at the game via a Netflix special this week. The company has not publicly acknowledged the rogue clips or commented at all.

en.title: Growing Pains' cast, over 40 years later: from an Oscar race to the kitchen to video games — see where they ended up
en.description: More than four decades after the Seavers first opened their Long Island front door to America and gave us laughs one half-hour at a time, the actor...
en.fullContent:
More than four decades after the Seavers first opened their Long Island front door to America and gave us laughs one half-hour at a time, the actors who portrayed the oh-so-lovable Growing Pains family are leading wildly different lives. However, the characters they played still come together in people's living rooms in reruns and through streaming services every day. The ABC sitcom ran for seven seasons from 1985 to 1992, and it turned a houseful of unknown actors into household names. Here's what the cast are doing today.

Tracey Gold at the ABC Summer Press Tour Party 2004 on July 13, 2004 in Century City, California. Tracey Gold, who played bookish middle child Carol Seaver, has become an advocate and speaker on eating-disorder recovery.

Tracey Gold, who portrayed smart, bookish middle child Carol Seaver, was a fan-favorite character, and she brought a lot of sensitivity to the show. Carol is in her early teens and a freshman in high school at the start of the first season, and audiences saw her grow up on screen.

Early in the show, Carol was teased mercilessly by her brother Mike, but in retrospect it's very disturbing to view the scenes with "size jokes" directed towards the young teen. During the later years of the show's run, she openly battled anorexia nervosa, and it tragically became tabloid fodder. She later told Oprah that it was hard for her that the show ended while she was still battling the disease, and she shared that she faked eating pizza in the last scene of Growing Pains.

Tracey Gold has since turned that hard chapter into a way to help others. Back in 2003, she wrote the memoir, Room to Grow: An Appetite for Life, with Julie McCarron, in which Gold opened up about her struggle with anorexia, and it also chronicles her eventual recovery. The book is still available in hardcover, paperbank, and as a Kindle e-book.

Gold also starred in the made-for-TV movie, For the Love of Nancy, in 1994. It was about a young woman's battle with anorexia and how her whole family deals with it. Jill Clayburgh portrayed her mother in the film, and it was a good, honest depiction of a very tough topic. In 2011, she was still raising awareness, and she hosted a documentary series called Starving Secrets with Tracey Gold. The show followed 10 girls as they dealt with their eating disorders in treatment centers.
